title: Signature Census Source Catalog — Catalog Overview
body:
This is the Signature edition overview of the Census Source Catalog. It is a Signature-compiled companion record that explains the catalog and how a Signature reader uses it. It describes the catalog endpoint itself, which is a real public service, and it does not claim that any dataset listed by the catalog has been harvested.

The Census Bureau developer page documents its public APIs and data products, covering demographic, housing, economic, and geographic statistics for the United States. This database catalogs those program areas: what each covers, how to query it, and how to reach it. It does not copy or claim any individual Census table or response.

Field 1 — Dataset title and stable identifier: Catalog title: Census Source Catalog. Stable identifier in this database: the record id shown on this record. The catalog home is https://www.census.gov/data/developers.html.

Field 2 — Publisher and responsible organization: Publisher: United States Census Bureau, United States Department of Commerce.

Field 3 — Original source URL and download or API endpoint: Original source URL: https://www.census.gov/data/developers.html. This is the single catalog home for this source family.

Field 4 — Subject categories and searchable description: Subject categories: all collection topics of this catalog, listed as the twelve dataset records of this database. Searchable description: The Census Bureau developer page documents its public APIs and data products, covering demographic, housing, economic, and geographic statistics for the United States. This database catalogs those program areas: what each covers, how to query it, and how to reach it. It does not copy or claim any individual Census table or response.

Field 5 — Geographic coverage and jurisdiction: Geographic coverage and jurisdiction: the full coverage of the catalog, spanning every topic record in this database; see Field 5 of each topic record for topic coverage.

Field 6 — Date range, publication date, and last-checked timestamp: Date range: the catalog is a living index with no single date range. Publication date: the catalog is continuously published. Last-checked timestamp for this catalog record: 2026-10-25.

Field 7 — Update frequency and freshness status: Update frequency and freshness status: Update frequency varies by program, from annual survey releases to decennial census releases and monthly estimates; the developer page states the schedule for each program. The catalog index itself is updated as publishers register or update datasets.

Field 8 — Schema, field definitions, data types, and units: Schema, field definitions, data types, and units: the catalog entry schema, not any dataset schema. Catalog entries generally carry a title, description, publisher, keywords, dates, and access links; exact fields vary by catalog and are shown on the catalog home.

Field 9 — License, attribution, and reuse restrictions: License, attribution, and reuse restrictions: United States federal government works are generally in the public domain in the United States; Census Bureau data products carry citation guidance on the developer page, so cite the Bureau as the source.

Field 10 — Authentication, quotas, and access limitations: Authentication, quotas, and access limitations: The developer documentation is openly readable; Census API use is open for modest use and a free key raises rate limits, as stated on the developer page.

Field 11 — Data format and file size: Data format and file size: the catalog is a search index and metadata service, not a single downloadable file. File size: varies by dataset — see catalog entry.

Field 12 — Provenance and upstream relationships: Provenance and upstream relationships: this overview derives from the public description of the catalog itself. Upstream, the catalog aggregates or lists dataset descriptions from the publishers named in Field 2.

Field 13 — Record count and completeness: Record count and completeness: this database holds 14 records: this overview, 12 collection-topic records, and 1 retrieval guide. Catalog-wide dataset counts are not measured — see catalog entry, and no catalog-wide count is claimed here.

Field 14 — Quality checks, known errors, and validation status: Quality checks, known errors, and validation status: this overview has been checked for the honesty rules of this database: no invented identifier, link, count, or file size appears in it. The catalog service itself was not load-tested for this record.

Field 15 — Version history and change detection: Version history and change detection: the catalog service changes as publishers add or update entries; re-check the catalog home to detect changes. This overview carries last-checked date 2026-10-25.

Field 16 — Duplicate relationships: Duplicate relationships: the twelve topic records in this database overlap by design, because catalog topics are browsing aids. The Signature edition of this database mirrors the public edition topic for topic and is the companion, not a duplicate, record.

Field 17 — Privacy classification and access controls: Privacy classification and access controls: public catalog overview. This record contains no personal data and describes no individual.

Field 18 — Retrieval instructions and sample queries: Retrieval instructions and sample queries: Open the developer page, find the program area in the API documentation, and search the collection topic name given in Field 18 of each record. Start at the catalog home https://www.census.gov/data/developers.html and browse or search by topic name.

Field 19 — Citation format and exact source references: Citation format and exact source references: cite the catalog home https://www.census.gov/data/developers.html with access date 2026-10-25, and cite this database record by its record id.

Field 20 — Status: available. This record describes the catalog endpoint itself, which is a public service; dataset ingestion status for individual topics is given in Field 20 of each topic record.

TOPIC = "catalog overview"
print('Search ' + CATALOG + ' for: ' + TOPIC)

title: Signature Census Source Catalog — Retrieval Guide
body:
This is the Signature edition retrieval guide for the Census Source Catalog. It is a Signature-compiled companion record that explains, step by step, how a Signature reader queries the catalog, builds search links, and checks that a catalog record carries all twenty required fields. It describes the catalog endpoint itself and does not claim that any dataset has been harvested.

Step 1: open the catalog home at https://www.census.gov/data/developers.html. Step 2: use the catalog search box and search a topic name from this database, or browse the catalog topic list. Step 3: open a dataset entry and read its full catalog page, including its license, schema, update frequency, and access link. Step 4: follow the entry stated download or API link, honoring any key or quota note on that entry. Step 5: record the dataset title, publisher, catalog entry address, and access date in your own citation, so the retrieval can be repeated.

Reproducibility notes: catalog listings change as publishers add, update, or withdraw entries, so re-run the same search on a later date and compare the entry list to detect change. Record the access date with every citation. If an entry disappears, its publisher page, not this database, is the authority on whether the dataset moved or was withdrawn. Sample queries: search each of the twelve topic names in this database, one at a time, and note the entry count shown by the catalog for that search; do not copy any count into this database without re-checking it.

Demo result: the retrieval-guide demo program below builds a catalog search link from the catalog home and checks a twenty-field sample record for completeness. Its stored output is: catalog: https://www.census.gov/data/developers.html | topics: 12 | search example: https://www.census.gov/data/developers.html/?search=Decennial%20Census | fields required: 20 | fields missing in sample: 0 | completeness: PASS.

Field 1 — Dataset title and stable identifier: Guide title: Retrieval guide for the Census Source Catalog. Stable identifier in this database: the record id shown on this record.

Field 2 — Publisher and responsible organization: Publisher: United States Census Bureau, United States Department of Commerce.

Field 3 — Original source URL and download or API endpoint: Original source URL: https://www.census.gov/data/developers.html.

Field 4 — Subject categories and searchable description: Subject categories: retrieval methods for all twelve collection topics of this catalog. Searchable description: how to search, query, download, and cite entries from this catalog.

Field 5 — Geographic coverage and jurisdiction: Geographic coverage and jurisdiction: the full coverage of the catalog; see Field 5 of each topic record.

Field 6 — Date range, publication date, and last-checked timestamp: Date range: not applicable to a guide. Publication date: this guide was written for the catalog as checked on 2026-10-25. Last-checked timestamp: 2026-10-25.

Field 7 — Update frequency and freshness status: Update frequency and freshness status: re-check this guide against the catalog home whenever the catalog changes its search interface; otherwise the steps remain valid.

Field 8 — Schema, field definitions, data types, and units: Schema, field definitions, data types, and units: the twenty-field record standard of this database, listed in the demo program: title, publisher, source URL, categories, coverage, dates, frequency, schema, license, authentication, format, provenance, count, quality, versions, duplicates, privacy, retrieval, citation, and status.

Field 9 — License, attribution, and reuse restrictions: License, attribution, and reuse restrictions: United States federal government works are generally in the public domain in the United States; Census Bureau data products carry citation guidance on the developer page, so cite the Bureau as the source.

Field 10 — Authentication, quotas, and access limitations: Authentication, quotas, and access limitations: The developer documentation is openly readable; Census API use is open for modest use and a free key raises rate limits, as stated on the developer page.

Field 11 — Data format and file size: Data format and file size: this guide is a text record. Catalog data formats: Formats vary by product and commonly include JSON API responses, CSV downloads, and downloadable data files. File size: varies by dataset — see catalog entry.

Field 12 — Provenance and upstream relationships: Provenance and upstream relationships: this guide derives from the public documentation of the catalog itself and from the twelve topic records of this database.

Field 13 — Record count and completeness: Record count and completeness: this guide covers all 14 records of this database and all 12 of its topics. Catalog-wide dataset counts are not measured — see catalog entry.

Field 14 — Quality checks, known errors, and validation status: Quality checks, known errors, and validation status: the demo program in this record was actually executed at build time and its output is stored on this record; re-execution must reproduce it. No dataset-level validation is claimed.

Field 15 — Version history and change detection: Version history and change detection: if the catalog changes its search interface, this guide must be revised and re-dated; until then it stands as checked on 2026-10-25.

Field 16 — Duplicate relationships: Duplicate relationships: this guide overlaps the overview record in describing the catalog, by design: the overview describes the catalog, this guide describes using it.

Field 17 — Privacy classification and access controls: Privacy classification and access controls: public guide. This record contains no personal data and describes no individual.

Field 18 — Retrieval instructions and sample queries: Retrieval instructions and sample queries: Open the developer page, find the program area in the API documentation, and search the collection topic name given in Field 18 of each record. Sample searches: one search per topic name in this database, plus a search for the catalog name itself on its own home page.

Field 19 — Citation format and exact source references: Citation format and exact source references: cite the catalog home https://www.census.gov/data/developers.html with access date, plus the dataset entry you actually opened, plus this guide by record id.

Field 20 — Status: available. This record describes the catalog query method itself; individual dataset ingestion status is given in Field 20 of each topic record.
demo_code:
CATALOG_HOME = "https://www.census.gov/data/developers.html"
TOPICS = ["Decennial Census", "American Community Survey One-Year", "American Community Survey Five-Year", "Population Estimates", "Economic Census", "Annual Business Survey", "County Business Patterns", "Housing Vacancies and Homeownership", "International Programs", "Geographic Codes and Boundaries", "Business Dynamics", "Income, Poverty, and Small Area Estimates"]
FIELDS = ["Dataset title and stable identifier", "Publisher and responsible organization", "Original source URL and download or API endpoint", "Subject categories and searchable description", "Geographic coverage and jurisdiction", "Date range, publication date, and last-checked timestamp", "Update frequency and freshness status", "Schema, field definitions, data types, and units", "License, attribution, and reuse restrictions", "Authentication, quotas, and access limitations", "Data format and file size", "Provenance and upstream relationships", "Record count and completeness", "Quality checks, known errors, and validation status", "Version history and change detection", "Duplicate relationships", "Privacy classification and access controls", "Retrieval instructions and sample queries", "Citation format and exact source references", "Status"]
from urllib.parse import quote

def search_url(home, query):
    # Helper that builds a starting search link from the catalog home
    # plus the query term; use the catalog own search box to refine it.
    return home.rstrip('/') + '/?search=' + quote(query)

def check_record(record):
    missing = [f for f in FIELDS if not record.get(f)]
    return missing

sample = {f: 'present' for f in FIELDS}
missing = check_record(sample)
print('catalog: ' + CATALOG_HOME)
print('topics: ' + str(len(TOPICS)))
print('search example: ' + search_url(CATALOG_HOME, TOPICS[0]))
print('fields required: ' + str(len(FIELDS)))
print('fields missing in sample: ' + str(len(missing)))
print('completeness: ' + ('PASS' if not missing else 'FAIL'))
demo_output:
catalog: https://www.census.gov/data/developers.html
topics: 12
search example: https://www.census.gov/data/developers.html/?search=Decennial%20Census
fields required: 20
fields missing in sample: 0
completeness: PASS
provenance: Retrieval guide compiled from the public catalog documentation; demo executed at build; last-checked 2026-10-25.
